title: Capability scorecard: Qwen 3.8 Max, Flash and 27B on Modality
evidence_policy: Existing artifacts only; no new runs or paid calls. Ratings describe recorded behaviour, not causes of score gaps (see docs/research/qwen-modality-claim-audit-20261015.md).
caveats: One recorded run per model and condition; not success rates.
Baseline+ and AVO differ in tools, budgets, instructions and output; not a matched comparison.
The 27B baseline+ run dates from 8 Oct; the Max and Flash baseline+ runs from 13 Oct.
Level 4 is not held out: its initial board was visible at the end of Max's research, and self-check 2 played it before final evaluation.
Ratings are one analyst's reading; no second annotator has checked them.
Offline ablations are simulator results, not real-service reruns.

summary.Max: Good at perception, controls, predictive modelling, planning and real self-checks. Its rules are still imperfect (grey treated as a global phase; the discriminating test was never run). In baseline+ it misread the goal and credited its win to the wrong cause.
summary.Flash: Good at goal recognition, credit assignment and finding undo in direct play; found a near-exact colour rule in research. Weak at consolidating: no written rules, a re-learning solver without real self-checks, and a level-2 loop. The cause of its 1/4 is not isolated.
summary.27B: Weakest at the start of the pipeline: reads the older frame and misreads undo, then builds hidden-state rules that agree with its own misreading. Eventually forms the right goal hypothesis and runs structured experiments; its solvers loop on no-ops and the recent run made no real checks.

interventions.name: Enforced real self-check before finish
interventions.description: Reserve wall time; the harness runs evaluate_solver automatically if the model has not, then returns the result for at least one repair turn.
interventions.evidence: Max used 2 checks (check 1 caught a crash); Flash and 27B used 0 and timed out mid-edit. The 30 Sep 27B run used checks and still did not solve, so checks are not sufficient on their own.

test.harness: AVO + check gate vs current AVO

interventions.name: Latest-frame-only observation API
interventions.description: Return only the post-action frame, or label frames explicitly as before/after.
interventions.evidence: The 27B parser reads frame[0] and builds delayed-action theories; the offline parser patch alone scored 1/4, so this tests learning from clean observations, not repairing the old solver.

interventions.name: Rival-hypothesis step with a discriminating probe
interventions.description: For each surprising transition, list at least two explanations (including undo/reset and local vs global causes) and choose the action that tells them apart.
interventions.evidence: Max never separated global phase from local compatibility (32/1,060 wrong); 27B read undo as a jump; Flash's rules stayed edge-local in baseline+.

test.harness: baseline+ (100 actions) with step vs control

interventions.name: Supplied action meanings
interventions.description: Say that ACTION1-4 are directions and ACTION7 is undo; rules and goal stay hidden.
interventions.evidence: 27B baseline+ jump theory led to 'No reset exists' after a recoverable deadlock.

interventions.name: Supplied goal
interventions.description: State that the goal is to put the crate on the target.
interventions.evidence: Max baseline+ treated the crate as a door; 27B confirmed the goal only late.

interventions.name: Consolidate research into the solver
interventions.description: Require writing confirmed rules into world_model.md and building the solver on the validated research model.
interventions.evidence: Flash's research plan.py held the right movement rule, but its notes were unchanged and its solver re-learned online. Whether this caused its 1/4 is untested.

interventions.name: Supplied true mechanics plus a planner (diagnostic ceiling)
interventions.description: Supply the true rules, used with the model's own planner or a deterministic one; any gap that remains points to planning or implementation.
interventions.evidence: Flash and 27B solvers loop even with partly correct rules.

interventions.name: No-op watchdog and an explicit policy for unknown moves
interventions.description: Force a replan or probe after k position no-ops. Variant A treats unverified moves as blocked; variant B leaves them unknown and probes them explicitly.
interventions.evidence: 27B: 1,405 no-ops; Flash: a 740/736 loop. There is a tension: Max's conservative but wrong model still won, Flash found that treating untested objects as blockers stopped the push to the target, and the proposal's ledger says unknown moves must not be recorded as walls.

test.harness: offline replay of saved solvers with the watchdog first ($0); then AVO x3 if trajectories change

cost_basis: Max about $20/run ($6/M output; input-dominated). Flash/27B AVO runs used 22-34M input and 0.5-0.7M output tokens; at $0.47/M output, output costs under $0.40; the Alibaba input price is not recorded in the repo, so the estimate is ~$1-10/run. Baseline+ Flash/27B ~$1-2/run.
